entities.summary: Af\u02fdal al-D\u03b2n Maraq\u05dc K\u062f \u062c\u0627sh\u0627n\u06cc, also known as Baba Afzal, was a Persian poet and philosopher of the Classical era. Born in Persia during the Seljuk Empire (c. 1180s), he was influenced by the works of Rumi and Hafez, and his own poetry explored themes of love, spirituality, and social justice. Kashani's poetry was widely circulated among Sufi communities and was praised for its beauty, depth, and emotional resonance. His legacy continued to inspire Persian literature and Sufi thought for centuries, influencing famous writers such as Rumi's grandson, Sultan Walad, and the renowned poet, Hafiz of Shiraz. Kashani's poetry also reflected his strong sense of social justice, addressing issues like poverty, inequality, and the exploitation of the poor. His most famous poem, 'The Eulogy of Love', is still widely read and studied today, and his influence can be seen in the works of modern Persian writers and artists.
